notes: The sheet is a typescript with handwritten mathematical signs, two squares, interlinear additions, cancellation strokes, and a slanted left marginal note. It begins in continuation with de Kostant and ends during der-. No title, date, or authorial page counter is visible. The lower-left 18 is treated as archive numbering and retained only in a TeX comment.

The opening describes maps from Dyn_c to ST_c and Un_c, a map supplied by Deligne to the underlined slashed-oval object, and their square. The small handwritten square has L and P on the left and overwritten Z_o and a looped z-like letter applied to e on the right. Its interpretation as a stabilizer square is not inserted into the transcription.

The long paragraph states a criterion for rational points, chooses a Levi subgroup and a one-parameter subgroup, and asserts that suitable u=exp(e) form a dense open subset of the handwritten g(2)-like object. This is a description of what is written, not an independent proof.

The handwritten replacement reads que G est quasi-déployé. The old typed condition, its terminal semicolon, les i, point rationnel, i.e, aux, est donc non vide, the p under marche, and fib are all preserved in their source states. The final dot after the cancelled i.e remains live.

The source explicitly hesitates: il n'est pas clair que cette propriété, with the addition de c, follows from invariance of c prime, faute de savoir si c mapsto c prime est injectif sur les classes de Dynkin. The margin says Il n'est en effet pas le cas, p.ex. pour A_2,A_4 (cela l'est pour A_3); the exact grammatical referent of this note is not supplied editorially.

The semi-local remark retains the provisional limitation de car. nulle jusqu'à nouvel ordre. The next paragraph asks whether the stabilizer in Autext(G_o) is the same as that of the corresponding Dynkin classes, et pas str. plus grand. No affirmative answer is inserted.

The wording de cette classe rationnel is preserved despite its potentially awkward agreement. The bottom word is left as der with C's continuation convention; a comment records the physical line-end hyphen.

The opening two cells and the des/les cell before questions contain mixed contours. Their chronology is not reconstructed from grammar. Likewise the blackened Z in the small square is drawn with its extra strokes without inventing a readable predecessor.

Every capital in the supplied functor-name formula groups was checked on its targeted crop: first Dyn, first ST and Un, Deligne Un, main-square ST/CL/Dyn/Par/Un, the cancelled Dyn, paragraph Par and Dyn, and Autext with G. None showed a definite separable same-letter double impression. Their ordinary alphabets are retained; darkness alone was not used to infer mathbb.

The two marks after si are kept doubtful as colon versus one-sided quotation strokes. No balancing quotation mark was added. The numeric 2 trace in the handwritten Lie-algebra expression and the shorthand after au remain locally doubtful.
